scope.label: Bronisław Kaper early career, documented through 1939

records.publicNote: Kaper’s birthplace and the main city of his education and early musical activity before his move to Berlin.
Berlin was Kaper’s principal city during his German period, associated with his studies, cabaret and publishing networks, and early film work.
Kaper’s main place of activity after leaving Germany in 1933 and before his move to the United States.
Los Angeles provides the metropolitan context for Kaper’s Hollywood career after his move to MGM.
Hollywood is used here as the district associated with Kaper’s American film career.

Historic MGM studio complex in Culver City associated with Kaper’s MGM career and Hollywood film work. The marker represents the studio site as a whole; the surviving evidence does not identify a particular stage, office or entrance for the linked events.

Warsaw address associated with Kaper in university and police documentation. The tenement, designed by Henryk Stifelman and Stanisław Weiss, was partly demolished and substantially rebuilt after 1945; its post-war condition is documented in the files of the Capital City Reconstruction Office (APW, file 5069).
The University of Warsaw is associated with Kaper’s law studies. The marker identifies the historic central campus; it does not claim a particular Faculty of Law room or classroom.

records.displayName: Stanisław Staszic Gymnasium, Polna 60 / Noakowskiego 6, Warsaw
records.authorizedName: Gimnazjum im. Stanisława Staszica w Warszawie, ul. Polna 60
records.publicNote: The Staszic school was associated with Kaper’s secondary education and matura. Its building at Polna 60 was completed in 1916, after the start of the 1915/16 school year; the site is linked to his transfer as the school’s later home, not as a confirmed location of the transfer. Part of Polna Street was renamed for Stanisław Noakowski in 1938, giving the same site the address Noakowskiego 6. Warszawa1939.pl documents it under the later address and cites a history using both forms. Burned after the Warsaw Uprising, the building was rebuilt and given an additional storey. The coordinates indicate the address area.

records.displayName: Chopin School of Music, Warsaw Philharmonic building, Jasna 5
records.authorizedName: Wyższa Szkoła Muzyczna im. Fryderyka Chopina przy Warszawskim Towarzystwie Muzycznym, gmach Filharmonii Warszawskiej, ul. Jasna 5, Warsaw
records.publicNote: Fryderyk Chopin Higher School of Music at the Warsaw Music Society, associated with Kaper’s piano studies and housed in the Warsaw Philharmonic building at Jasna 5. The marker identifies the documented building site, not a specific classroom.
The church is connected with the record of Kaper’s baptism in 1920.
Culver City is the location of the MGM studios where Kaper worked during his Hollywood career.

Hamborn, in the Ruhr area, was the setting of the ERKLA concert reviewed in December 1929. The review named Kaper alongside Giuliano Pomeranz, then performing as Julian Pomeranc, Alexander Zakin and Leopold Mittmann.
Sienna 44 is associated with Kaper’s birthplace in Warsaw. The coordinates indicate the address area; exact continuity between the 1902 property and the modern address point remains unverified.

records.displayName: A. M. Skrynnikow Real School, Żórawia 49, Warsaw
records.authorizedName: Szkoła realna A. M. Skrynnikowa w Warszawie, ul. Żórawia 49 / Żurawia 49
records.publicNote: Kaper attended this Warsaw school before transferring to the Staszic school. It was at ul. Żórawia 49, now Żurawia 49. The coordinates indicate the address area; survival of the historical school building has not been established.

records.displayName: Warsaw Conservatory Concert Hall, Okólnik 1, Warsaw
records.publicNote: Concert hall in the pre-war Warsaw Conservatory building at 1 Okólnik Street, associated with the 1928 press notices on Eliza Rozenblum’s performance of Kaper’s piano pieces. The coordinates indicate the conservatory site, not the exact hall point.

records.authorizedName: Filharmonia Warszawska / Warsaw Philharmonic, ul. Jasna 5
records.publicNote: The Warsaw Philharmonic was the venue of a Chopin Music School concert at which Kaper performed.

records.displayName: Teatr Morskie Oko, Jasna 3 / Sienkiewicza 7, Warsaw
records.publicNote: Warsaw revue theatre that opened in 1928 as a successor to Perskie Oko; Kaper’s “O tem wróble świergocą,” to words by Andrzej Włast, was sung in its revue Gwiazdy Warszawy. Morskie Oko occupied the corner of Jasna 3 and Sienkiewicza 7 from 1928 to 1933; that historical venue address is used for the map.

Historic cinema site at Kurfürstendamm 153, connected with the 1929 Bick & Kaper appearance at the premiere of Der Adjutant des Zaren. The marker identifies the documented venue site, not a position within the former auditorium.

On 23 December 1933 Paris-Soir reported Kaper and Jurmann at the Salabert recording studio in Montrouge. The studio’s exact street address has not been verified, so the map marker represents Montrouge at city level.

records.displayName: Hôtel George V, 31 avenue George V, Paris
records.authorizedName: Hôtel George V / Four Seasons Hotel George V, 31 avenue George-V, Paris
records.publicNote: This Paris hotel was the venue of a reception for Jan Kiepura attended by Kaper and Jurmann.
At this Paris hotel, Kaper and Jurmann reportedly met Louis B. Mayer before signing their MGM contract.
Kaper and Eleonora arrived in New York after crossing the Atlantic from Le Havre aboard the S.S. Champlain, before travelling on to Los Angeles.

records.authorizedName: French Line Pier 57, North River, foot of West 15th Street, Manhattan, New York
records.publicNote: Approximate arrival site for Kaper and Eleonora’s 1934 Atlantic crossing from Le Havre aboard the S.S. Champlain. In this period the French Line (Compagnie Générale Transatlantique) used Pier 57 on the North River, at the foot of West 15th Street; the pier is inferred from the line’s documented berth rather than named in the passenger manifest. The record establishes arrival at New York but not processing at Ellis Island.

Kaper sailed from Le Havre to New York aboard the S.S. Champlain in 1934. The marker is placed at city level. At the time, CGT liners used the port’s earlier transatlantic quays: the Gare Maritime on quai Johannès-Couvert opened in May 1935, with the Normandie, and was destroyed in the 1944 bombing of Le Havre.
Calexico was the U.S. border city through which Kaper entered for permanent residence in 1935.

Mexicali is the Baja California border city from which Kaper and Eleonora entered the United States at Calexico for permanent residence. The map marker uses official city-level coordinates and does not identify the location of the historical Commercial Hotel.

records.displayName: Château des Fleurs, 6626 Franklin Ave., Hollywood
records.authorizedName: Château des Fleurs, 6626 Franklin Avenue, Hollywood, Los Angeles
records.publicNote: French Norman Revival apartment building completed in 1927 and designated Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument no. 799. Kaper’s 1 November 1935 immigration manifest records 6626 Franklin Avenue as his U.S. destination, and his Declaration of Intention dated 4 February 1936 records the same address as his residence.

Vienna forms part of the European music and film context of Kaper’s Berlin–Paris–Hollywood route and the star-singer circuit. MGM’s later label “Viennese composers” does not describe Kaper’s place of origin.

Major German film-production centre associated with the multiple-language version system in early European sound cinema. The marker represents the broader historic Babelsberg studio complex; no individual stage or production building is asserted for the linked context.
Joinville was a French studio and production centre associated with multiple-language versions in early sound cinema.
Kaper lived on Pommersche Straße in Wilmersdorf, a residential district in western Berlin, before his departure in 1933.

Documented Berlin residence: the Berliner Adreßbuch 1932 lists B. Kaper, composer, at Pommersche Straße 3 in Wilmersdorf. A later official planning record identifies the historical corner parcel as Sächsische Straße 48–49 / Pommersche Straße 3–4. Numbers 3–4 are absent from the present official address register, so the marker locates the historical corner parcel approximately rather than a surviving entrance.

records.displayName: Château Frontenac, 54 rue Pierre Charron, Paris
records.authorizedName: Hôtel Château Frontenac, 54 rue Pierre-Charron, Paris
records.publicNote: Kaper gave this Paris hotel as his home address on the S.S. Champlain passenger manifest before arriving in New York. It is interpreted here as a transit hotel address rather than a private residence.

records.displayName: Casino de Paris, 16 rue de Clichy, Paris
records.authorizedName: Casino de Paris, 16 rue de Clichy, Paris
records.publicNote: The Casino de Paris is part of the revue and music-hall context of the Jurmann–Kaper partnership in Paris in 1933/34.

records.displayName: Sievering Film Studio, Sieveringer Straße 135, Vienna
records.authorizedName: Sieveringer Filmatelier / Sievering Studios, Sieveringer Straße 135, 1190 Vienna-Döbling
records.publicNote: Historical film-studio site at Sieveringer Straße 135 in Vienna’s 19th district, Döbling. The studio complex operated at this address from the Sascha-Film era and no longer survives in its historical form.
Kaper later recalled a short trip to London at Sam Spiegel’s invitation for a projected Anthony Asquith film that did not materialise.

records.displayName: Commercial Hotel (formerly Hotel Aldrete), Madero at Azueta, Mexicali
records.authorizedName: Hotel Comercial (formerly Hotel Aldrete), Avenida Francisco I. Madero at Calle José Azueta, Mexicali, Baja California
records.publicNote: Kaper’s 1 November 1935 Calexico manifest records the Commercial Hotel in Mexicali as his last permanent residence abroad. Historical evidence identifies the Hotel Comercial as the renamed Hotel Aldrete on Avenida Francisco I. Madero, between Ayuntamiento and José Azueta, beside Parque Héroes de Chapultepec. The marker represents the documented site, not a verified 1935 street number.

records.displayName: Consulate General of the Republic of Poland, 19 rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Paris
records.authorizedName: Consulate General of the Republic of Poland in Paris, 19 rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Paris 17e
records.publicNote: Polish consular institution in Paris that issued Kaper’s Polish passport in August 1934, later noted in the Calexico border-crossing documentation. Historical address identified as 19 rue Alphonse-de-Neuville, Paris 17e.

records.authorizedName: Bach-Saal / former Blüthner-Saal, Lützowstraße 76 / Genthiner Straße 11 (today Genthiner Straße 26), Berlin-Tiergarten
records.publicNote: At this Berlin concert venue, Róża Etkin gave a recital on 3 December 1927 that included an unnamed work by B. Kaper. An advertisement described it as an Uraufführung, but the other surviving listing does not confirm that it was a first performance. The Bach-Saal was the former Blüthner-Saal, renamed after renovation in autumn 1927, in the Klindworth-Scharwenka / Schwalm hall complex at Lützowstraße 76 / Genthiner Straße. The marker represents the documented complex rather than a reconstructed footprint of the individual hall.

records.authorizedName: Kabarett der Komiker / KadeKo, probable July 1928 venue: Haus Cumberland / Palmenhaus, Kurfürstendamm 193–194, Berlin-Charlottenburg
records.publicNote: Berlin cabaret venue connected with Kaper’s paid work as a pianist. A July 1928 programme lists Sula Lewitsch and Bronisław Kaper as “Jazz auf zwei Klavieren”; because the event predates the later WOGA venue, Haus Cumberland / Palmenhaus at Kurfürstendamm 193–194 is retained as the probable site.

records.authorizedName: Calexico–Mexicali Port of Entry (Calexico, California / Mexicali, Baja California)
records.publicNote: Land border port of entry linking Calexico (California) and Mexicali (Baja California), documented as the point of Kaper and Eleonora’s 1935 permanent-residence entry into the United States. The coordinates mark the historic downtown crossing at the foot of Heffernan Avenue, where the 1933 inspection station stood in 1935; the vehicle crossing was moved two blocks west in 1974 and the present buildings are later.

A Montpellier summer-festival programme published on 22 June 1934 listed a jazz orchestra performing the Jurmann–Kaper song “Ninon, quand tu me souris” from Tout pour l’amour on an open-air stage. The programme documents the song’s circulation beyond cinema.

records.displayName: Hotel Edison, 228 West 47th Street, New York
records.authorizedName: Hotel Edison, 228 West 47th Street, New York, NY
records.publicNote: New York hotel where Kaper and his wife Eleonora stayed on arrival from Le Havre before travelling on to Los Angeles. In his 1975 AFI oral history Kaper recalled the Edison Hotel as the studio’s $300-a-week accommodation tier.

records.displayName: Teatr Perskie Oko, Nowy Świat 63, Warsaw
records.publicNote: Warsaw revue theatre founded by former members of Qui Pro Quo, where Zula Pogorzelska introduced Kaper’s first printed songs of 1926. Perskie Oko played at Nowy Świat 63 from 5 September 1925 to 11 September 1926, then at Marszałkowska 125 until August 1927. The coordinates give the modern address point of Nowy Świat 63; continuity with the pre-war building is not established.
